title: Working on a crazy swamp siege game with Glimp a glowtoad that can barf, spit and fart to avoid getting eaten.
author: xcantene
selftext:
hey everyone so this is the first trailer for Glimp Last Croak, been working on it for about 4 months now. 

its an idea I had in my head for a long time and after a lot of inspiration I finally just started making it. a really talented artist helped me find the vibe of the game in the beginning and that's what got me going on the pixel art myself. I lost my job somewhere in the middle of all this but I kept going with it anyway and honestly im pretty happy with where its at

the game is supposed to be crazy and silly and cute. you're Glimp a toad just trying to take a nap and not to get eaten by almost anyting in the world from waves and waves of monsters. right now there's 2 worlds base in the swamps with 12 levels, more than 10 kinds of monsters and 6 bosses. Glimp can spit bubbles, eat hot peppers and burp fire, throw goo, do a big croak wave and he can also fart to poison enemies! xD

there's towers too, I made carnivorous plants that turn into dragon plants, a reed that shoots little glowing wisps and a mushroom that spreads spores that grow more mushrooms

I've been trying to make the bosses fun with reactions too, like you have to press stuff at the right time to jump or dodge or slide down and dive under

I want to make 3 more worlds and a lot more upgrades and just way more stuff. so if you see this id love to hear for more craziest ideas for this crazy toad, what should he be able to do? what towers or bosses do you think I should make to try to eat him?

\-- 

How was AI involved into this?   
  
Opus 5.5 has helped me mostly on the review of the code and on balancing and running bots for testing. I also built my internal studio for the game where I can stored all m pixel art, preview them and work faster. Essentially where I can create pixel art in a more smart and faster way with the tools I needed to properly check frame by frame my animations and tweaks. Opus sometimes has helped me with some frames on which I had to of course edit.   
  
I also created a simple music studio to match the vibes and create my own original audios. Lately it has helped me on creating the perfect tool to capture the gameplay of bots and reproduce reels and trailers like the one you see on which I can quickly modify to save credits and type and tweak with its own animations that way I have to direct less the agent and I can focus on creating with just what I need! :)
